column2: The shareholders of Novo Nordisk have ultimate authority over the company and exercise their right to make decisions at general meetings. At the Annual General Meeting, shareholders approve the annual report and any amendments to the company's Articles of Association. Shareholders also elect Board members and the independent auditor. Resolutions can generally be passed by a simple majority.
column3: However, resolutions to amend the Articles of Association require two thirds of the votes cast and capital represented, unless other adoption requirements are imposed by the Danish Companies Act. Novo Holdings A/S holds the majority of votes at general meetings. However, allstrategic and operational maters are decided solely by the Board of Directors and Executive Management.

column2: Novo Nordisk has a two-tier management structure consisting of a Board of Directors and Executive Management. The two bodies are separate and no one serves as a member of both.
